title: Part-time community college student (with family, overnight warehouse, 3 classes, Canvas) is offered an extra Sunday night shift after Thanksgiving break that ends at 6:30 AM before her 10 AM Monday class.

changes.notes: Holiday peak extra shift. Reply to your lead by Wed noon if you can't.

dev_must_notice.what: Her employer posted an extra holiday-peak shift Sun Nov 29, 10 PM to 6:30 AM (x-peak-shift), posted at 12:05 PM today with 'reply to your lead by Wed noon if you can't'. It would be her fifth night in a row (shift-warehouse-2026-11-25, -26, -27 and -28, then this one) and it ends 6:30 AM Monday Nov 30, with BIO 105 at 10 AM and ENG 101 at noon (class-bio-105-2026-11-30, class-eng-101-2026-11-30) after break. Home at 6:55, her usual sleep after nights is 7:15 to 2:15 (m-day-sleep), so before the 10 AM class she would get 7:15 to 9:00, an hour and 45 minutes. She told Dev Sunday night is her one real night of sleep before Monday class (m-availability), and Sunday 6:30 to 7:45 PM is dinner with her mom and brothers (m-family). Thanksgiving dinner at her aunt's (x-thanksgiving, Thu 3 to 6 PM) already fits between her post-night sleep and her 10 PM shift; nothing to say about it.

best_fix.what: One push after her study block ends: 'Your lead posted an extra Sunday night shift, Nov 29, 10 PM to 6:30 AM. It would be five nights in a row and leave you 7:15 to 9:00 AM of sleep before BIO at 10. You reply by Wednesday noon. I wrote two replies you can send: [Say no, family dinner and class Monday] [Ask to leave at 3 AM]. Or skip both.' Dev does not decide for her, sends nothing, and says nothing about her saved unpaid time off. A second line Wednesday 11:00 AM (after her free-day sleep, before noon): 'Reply to your lead about Sunday by noon' only if she has not replied or chosen.
best_fix.why: It is a real choice with a clock on it (Wed noon) and she is the only one who can make it. Dev names the cost in her own facts (five nights, 1 h 45 min of sleep before class, Sunday dinner and her one real night of sleep) and makes either answer one tap, with her words in a draft she sends herself.

must_not: decide for her, accept or decline the shift, or message her lead
use or suggest her saved unpaid time off hours (m-upt) or skipping a class
suggest she study or sleep in the gap before Monday class so she can take the Sunday shift
count extra pay from the shift as money she has or predict her hourly pay
warn about Thanksgiving dinner at her aunt's (Thu 3 to 6 PM): it fits her sleep and her 10 PM shift
use guilt words or say she is overworking
send the push during her post-night sleep or her Tuesday study window (3 to 5:30 PM)
assumptions: The employer posts holiday-peak extra shifts the week before and asks for a reply by a set time; here Wed noon. She is not required to take it (typical for warehouse peak).
Her workweek starts Sunday, so the Sunday shift opens a new week of Sun Nov 29 plus Wed to Sat Dec 2 to 5, 40 paid hours with 30 minute unpaid breaks, no overtime. Dev says nothing about pay.

Wed Nov 25 is the first day of break and she has no class, so she is awake by about 10 AM after a free-day night; Tuesday's study block ends 5:30 PM, so 5:40 PM is the first calm moment after the posting.
Checking is $3,797.96 (pay of about $600 a week, a financial aid refund earlier); money is not part of this case.

tempting.suggestion: suggest she study or sleep in the gap before Monday class so she can take the Sunday shift
tempting.why_wrong: her post-night sleep is firm (7:15 AM to 2:15 PM) and the Sunday shift would leave her 1 h 45 min before class, so Dev does not engineer the shift to fit; it names the cost and lets her choose
